faq.label: Frequently asked
items: You see a demo of your own solution at the audit. The first system goes live within two to three weeks. We commit to the date in writing, before we start.
Development is a fixed fee. What is the subscription for?

Building your system is billed once, as a fixed fee agreed up front. The subscription covers what comes after: monitoring, fixes, updates and new work. Your software updates itself, AI models get replaced, your business changes — a system nobody watches eventually stops, often without anyone noticing straight away.
What if a workflow breaks on a Sunday?
An automation that fails does not announce it: it simply stops sending your follow-ups. That is why we monitor. You hear about it before your clients do, and the fix is part of the subscription.
Your systems run on your own infrastructure. Your data trains no public model, and you can see at any time which tool has access to what.
If we stop, do I lose everything?
No. What we build belongs to you and stays with you. You leave with your systems, with nothing to rebuild. That is the difference with software rented by the month.
Which tools do you work with?
Yours. We plug into your mailbox, your calendar, your CRM and your industry software. If you have no CRM, we work without one — and we will tell you plainly when you need one.
Thonon-les-Bains, on Lake Geneva. We travel across the Chablais, Évian, Annemasse and the Geneva basin, and work remotely everywhere else.

concerne.intro: The reform applies to every VAT-registered business established in France — including if you fall under the small-business exemption and charge no VAT. Only the issuing date changes with your size.
concerne.note: Business-to-business e-invoicing does not apply to you, but e-reporting does: your sales data still has to reach the tax authority through an approved platform.

risques.h2: The reform will not go away because you postponed it.

items.title: €50 per invoice, up to €15,000 a year
items.desc: The amount rose from €15 to €50 under the 2026 finance act. Every invoice issued outside the required format counts, and the cap runs per calendar year.

items.title: €500, then €1,000 every three months
items.desc: That is the fine for failing to designate an approved platform for receiving, once a formal notice has gone unanswered. It applies from 2026, whatever your size.

items.title: Supplier invoices stop reaching you
items.desc: Large companies and mid-caps issue electronically from September 2026. With no active platform, nothing from them reaches you, and your bookkeeping seizes up.

items.title: Over 150 platforms, and a decision to make
items.desc: The tax authority has registered more than 150, most of them provisionally pending an interoperability audit. Comparing formats, pricing and staying power takes time you do not have.

roadmap.h2: Five steps, run end to end.
roadmap.intro: You configure nothing on your own. We handle the technical side, you keep the decisions.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.desc: Thirty minutes to establish your status, your real deadlines and the state of your tools.

steps.title: Platform selection
steps.desc: Choosing and activating your approved platform, sized to your invoice volume.

steps.title: Connecting your tools
steps.desc: Invoicing, accounting, CRM: we wire up what you already run, no change of habits.

steps.title: Automating the flows
steps.desc: Issuing, receiving and e-reporting automated, for business and consumer customers alike.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.desc: We track the tax authority's publications and adjust your setup when the rules move.

automation.h2: While we are in there, you may as well stop keying invoices by hand.
automation.sub: Getting compliant means touching the whole invoicing chain. That is the moment to win back the time it costs you.
items: Invoice issued the moment a job or a sale ends, with no re-keying.
Payment chasers that send themselves, on a schedule you set once.
Consumer invoices generated and archived for e-reporting.
One dashboard: who owes you what, and for how long.
Audit-proof archiving, available if you are inspected.

offre.h2: Full compliance, handled end to end.
offre.name: E-invoicing Compliance Package
offre.intro: A one-off fee, no retainer, no subscription. The amount is set during the assessment, based on your situation.
items: Full assessment of your situation and deadlines
Selecting and activating your approved platform
Setting up e-reporting for your consumer sales
One hour of training on your new tool
Ninety days of follow-up and adjustments
offre.guarantee: The assessment is free and commits you to nothing. If it turns out you need nothing, we will say so.
offre.note: The approved platform's own fee is on you and depends on your invoice volume. We price it during the assessment.

pourquoi.h2: Support, not one more piece of software to work out alone.

items.title: One person, throughout
items.desc: No anonymous ticket queue. Whoever runs the assessment installs the setup and handles the follow-up.

items.title: Early beats the queue
items.desc: The closer the date, the more saturated platforms and integrators become. Dealing with it now costs less than in August 2026.

items.title: Compliance first, time saved next
items.desc: Automation is our core trade. Compliance is where the work starts, not where it ends.

items: I am under the small-business VAT exemption. Am I really covered?
Yes. The exemption means you are VAT-registered but not liable, so you stay within the scope of the reform. Receiving from 1 September 2026, issuing and e-reporting from 1 September 2027.
My issuing obligation only starts in 2027. Why act now?

Because the receiving obligation applies to everyone from September 2026. Your large and mid-cap suppliers will be issuing electronically by then: with no designated platform, their invoices never reach you and you are exposed to the €500 fine.
I only invoice consumers. Does this concern me?
Business-to-business e-invoicing does not apply to you, but e-reporting does: your sales data must reach the tax authority through an approved platform. So you still need one.
Is a PDF sent by email not enough?
No. Under the reform an electronic invoice is a structured file — Factur-X, UBL or CII — transmitted through an approved platform. A regular PDF, even signed, does not comply.
What do the ninety days of follow-up cover?
Any configuration fix, any question about how your platform behaves, and any adjustment made necessary by a change in the rules during the three months after go-live.

final.sub: Thirty minutes is enough to know where you stand and what is left to do.
